subject: maths
title: Pythagoras Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the most famous rule in maths — a² + b² = c² — and use it to find the hypotenuse.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths Pythagoras' Theorem foundations — the rule a²+b²=c², recognising the hypotenuse, and famous Pythagorean triples.
final_note: You can state Pythagoras' theorem, spot the hypotenuse and find it for whole-number triples like 3-4-5.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Pythagoras' theorem says: in any right-angled triangle, a² + b² = c².

Here a and b are the two short sides (the ones touching the 90° corner) and c is the hypotenuse — the longest side, opposite the right angle.

It only works for right-angled triangles. No 90°? No Pythagoras.

Before you start any Pythagoras question, find the hypotenuse:

• It's the longest side.
• It's opposite the right angle (it never touches it).
• It's always called c in the formula.

The other two sides are a and b. It doesn't matter which is which — addition is commutative (a² + b² = b² + a²).

Example: right-angled triangle, short sides 3 and 4. Find c.

c² = 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25, so c = √25 = 5.

This is the famous 3-4-5 triangle.

Worth memorising (Pythagorean triples):

• 3, 4, 5 → 9 + 16 = 25
• 5, 12, 13 → 25 + 144 = 169
• 8, 15, 17 → 64 + 225 = 289

Spot one in a question and the answer pops out without a calculator.

mcqs.q: In a² + b² = c², which side is c?
options: The shortest side
Any side you choose
The hypotenuse (longest, opposite the right angle)
The side along the bottom

mcqs.q: Pythagoras' theorem only works for triangles that have a:
options: 60° angle
right (90°) angle
pair of equal sides
pair of parallel sides

mcqs.q: In Pythagoras' theorem, which side does c^2 represent?
options: The angle at the centre is half the angle at the circumference.
c^2 represents any side of the triangle as long as the other two are squared.
c^2 represents the side opposite the largest angle that is not 90 degrees.
The hypotenuse — the longest side, opposite the right angle.

mcqs.q: Can Pythagoras' theorem be used on any triangle?
options: Yes — it works on any triangle as long as you square the sides.
Only on equilateral triangles because all sides are equal.
The angle at the centre is half the angle at the circumference.
No — it only applies to right-angled triangles.

mcqs.q: What is the relationship between the angle at the centre and the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc?
options: The angle at the centre is half the angle at the circumference.
The angles are equal because they are subtended by the same arc.
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.
Only on equilateral triangles because all sides are equal.

options: Whole numbers a, b, c with a² + b² = c².
Another triple: 25 + 144 = 169 = 13².
Classic right triangle: 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5².
Longest side, opposite the right angle.

Another triple: 25 + 144 = 169 = 13².
